P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No restrictive exchange controls on receiving foreign income (see quoted source); banks apply normal AML/KYC checks.

sources.title: United Kingdom Country Commercial Guide — Trade Financing
sources.quote: Foreign Exchange Controls There are no exchange controls restricting the transfer of funds into or out of the UK, although anyone carrying the equivalent of £10,000 or more in cash when entering the UK must declare it.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. UK banks offer personal foreign-currency accounts. HSBC UK's Currency Account lets you choose from 14 major currencies, with a separate account for each, to store, send and receive money; there is no monthly fee, and an HSBC UK current account is required (HSBC). Wise's comparison also lists HSBC's Global Money Account (18 currencies), NatWest's Cash Management Account and Barclays' Foreign Currency Account.

sources.title: Currency Account
sources.quote: You can choose from 14 major currencies and open a separate account for each one to store, send and receive money.

sources.title: Best multi-currency accounts you can open in the UK
sources.quote: To apply for the account, you’ll need to have an active HSBC UK current account .

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: You can start trading as a sole trader straight away without registering. You must register with HMRC for Self Assessment once you earn more than £1,000 in a tax year (6 April to 5 April) — the trading allowance — and then file Self Assessment returns.

L2_tax_id.answer: Official TIN description supplied by United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to the OECD: "The United K ingdom does not issue TINs in a strict sense, but it does have two TIN -like numbers, which are not reported on official documents of identification: 1. The unique taxpayer reference (UTR). The format is a unique set of 10 numerals allocated automatically by HMRC for both individuals and entities who have to submit a tax return." L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Graduated rates with a GBP 12,570 personal allowance (2026/27); statutory residence test; remittance basis abolished. Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income (see quoted rules). Work performed while living in United Kingdom for foreign clients is generally taxable there. Self-employed people also pay Class 4 National Insurance: 6% on profits from £12,570 to £50,270 and 2% above (2026/27).

sources.title: United Kingdom - Individual - Residence
sources.quote: The application of this test is of even greater relevance following the abolition of the remittance basis of taxation and a move to a residence-based regime.

sources.quote: For tax year 2026 to 2027 you’ll pay: 6% on profits over £12,570 up to £50,270 2% on profits over £50,270 You can see National Insurance rates for past tax years .

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 20% (5% reduced). Registration is compulsory when VAT-taxable turnover goes over £90,000; zero-rated sales count toward it. Register within 30 days of the end of the month you went over. Voluntary registration is possible below the threshold. Small traders (under £150,000) may use the flat-rate scheme. Services to overseas business customers are generally outside the scope of UK VAT (not captured).

sources.quote: The standard VAT rate of 20% applies to most goods and services, apart from domestic fuel and power and certain other reduced-rate supplies, which are subject to VAT at 5%.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Data protection is governed by the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, regulated by the ICO. Most businesses processing personal data must pay the ICO data protection fee (not captured).

sources.title: Data protection
sources.quote: In the UK, data protection is governed by the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and the Data Protection Act 2018 .

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: For distance (online) sales, consumers can cancel within 14 days of receiving goods, then have another 14 days to return them. The seller must refund within 14 days of receiving the item back.

sources.title: Accepting returns and giving refunds
sources.quote: They have another 14 days to return the item once they’ve told you.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: The £1,000 trading allowance means small side income under £1,000 a year needs no registration or tax (see L1). The VAT flat-rate scheme is available for small traders (see L4).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: none of the major platform barriers apply. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (6) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Fully localized'). (7) Stripe accepts merchants here, so you can take card payments directly on your own site. (8) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
